questions.question: Words or expressions used in a special, imaginative, or non-literal way to make writing interesting are called ________________.
A comparison between two different things using 'like' or 'as' is called a ________________.
Which figure of speech is used in: 'The baby is as gentle as a lamb'?
Identify the figure of speech: 'He runs like the wind.'
A direct comparison between two things without using 'like' or 'as' is called a ________________.
Which figure of speech is used in: 'Time is a thief'?
Identify the figure of speech: 'My sister is the sunshine of our home.'
Giving human qualities or actions to animals, objects, or ideas is called ________________.
Which figure of speech is used in: 'The wind whispered through the trees'?
Identify the figure of speech: 'The sun smiled at us.'
An extreme exaggeration used for emphasis that is not meant literally is called ________________.
Which figure of speech is used in: 'I have told you a million times'?
Identify the figure of speech: 'This bag weighs a ton.'
Words that imitate or suggest real sounds are called ________________.
Which figure of speech is used in: 'The clock went tick-tock'?
Identify the figure of speech: 'The bees buzzed around the flowers.'
The repetition of the same beginning consonant sound in nearby words is called ________________.
Which figure of speech is used in: 'Peter picked purple plums'?
The repetition of similar vowel sounds in nearby words is called ________________.
Which figure of speech is used in: 'Go slow over the road'?
The repetition of consonant sounds within or at the ends of nearby words is called ________________.
Joining two words with apparently opposite meanings together is called an ________________.
Which figure of speech is used in: 'Deafening silence filled the room'?
A statement that appears contradictory at first but reveals a truth, such as 'Less is more', is called a ________________.
Saying 'What lovely weather!' during a terrible storm is an example of ________________.
A play on words using multiple meanings or similar sounds, such as 'The maths teacher has too many problems', is a ________________.
A mild or polite expression used instead of one that sounds harsh, such as 'He passed away', is called ________________.
Replacing the name of something with a closely associated thing, such as 'The pen is mightier than the sword', is called ________________.
Using a part to represent the whole, such as 'All hands were needed on deck', is called ________________.
Addressing an absent person or a non-human thing directly, such as 'O Death, where is your sting?', is called ________________.
Choose the suitable prefix to form the opposite of 'Legal': ________________.
Choose the suitable prefix to form the opposite of 'Balance': ________________.
Choose the suitable prefix to form the opposite of 'Correct': ________________.
Choose the suitable prefix to form the opposite of 'Agree': ________________.
Choose the suitable prefix to form the opposite of 'Logical': ________________.
Form a noun from the adjective 'Able': ________________.
Form a noun from the verb 'Arrive': ________________.
Form a noun from the verb 'Decide': ________________.
Form a noun from the adjective 'Strong': ________________.
Form a noun from the verb 'Succeed': ________________.
Form an adjective from the noun 'Beauty': ________________.
Form an adjective from the noun 'Courage': ________________.
Form an adjective from the noun 'Danger': ________________.
Form a verb from the adjective 'Pure': ________________.
Form an adverb from the adjective 'Brave': ________________.
A group of words that contains a subject and a verb (or predicate) is called a ________________.
What are the two main kinds of clauses?
A clause that can stand alone by itself and make complete sense is called a ________________ clause.
A clause that cannot stand alone to make complete sense and relies on the main clause is a ________________ clause.
Which type of subordinate clause describes a noun or pronoun in the main clause and begins with who, which, or that?
Identify the type of subordinate clause in: 'This is the boy who stole the biro.'
Which type of clause performs the function of an adverb by telling how, when, where, or why an action occurred?
Identify the type of adverbial clause in: 'The students stopped talking when the principal entered.'
Identify the type of adverbial clause in: 'He came here because he needed some help.'
Identify the type of adverbial clause in: 'Kangaroos go wherever they can get food.'
Identify the type of adverbial clause in: 'He spoke to me as if he was mad.'
Which type of clause takes the place of a noun and functions as the subject or object of a verb?
A group of words that does NOT contain a finite verb and cannot form a major sentence on its own is called a ________________.
Which of the following is an example of a phrase?
Why is 'A loaf of bread' classified as a phrase rather than a clause?
options: It contains no subject-verb combination or finite verb
It starts with a capital letter
questions.answer: It contains no subject-verb combination or finite verb
